name: Verify Before Claiming Done
description: Always run commands and check actual output before claiming work is complete or tests pass.
content:
# Verify Before Claiming Done Rules

- Never say "done", "fixed", "implemented", or "tests pass" without actual command output in the same message
- Run the build command (`npm run build`, `cargo build`, `go build`) and verify exit code 0 before claiming success
- Run the full test suite and check the actual pass/fail counts — don't rely on previous run results
- Run the linter and verify 0 errors — don't assume clean output from memory
- If you say "should work", "probably fixed", or "seems correct" — stop and run the actual verification command
- Check that new files actually exist on disk after creating them — `ls` the path to confirm
- After fixing a bug, reproduce the original error first, apply the fix, then verify the error is gone
- After a git commit, run `git status` to confirm the working tree is clean
- After deploying, verify the deployment is live — check the URL, run a health check, or tail the logs
- When running multiple verification steps, complete all of them before declaring done — partial verification is not verification
- If a command fails, do not claim you will fix it later — fix it now and re-verify
- Show the evidence — paste the actual command output, exit code, or test results in your response
